action.content:
Pilot knowledge teams; retain five-day coverage for shift teams while testing service and staffing effects. [studies/nordvik_2025.md] [studies/harlow_2025.md]

Nordvik’s randomized, peer-reviewed knowledge-work trial found output per employee -0.4% (not significant), output per actual hour +5.9%, fewer sick days and attrition falling from 14% to 10%. Actual hours fell less than contracted hours, limiting a literal 32-hour interpretation. [studies/nordvik_2025.md]

Harlow’s non-peer-reviewed, self-selected mixed-workforce study found unchanged aggregate output but knowledge output +5.2% and customer-support output -8.7%; waits rose 31%. Wellbeing and retention improved, but shift coverage is a material constraint. [studies/harlow_2025.md]

Discount the retracted Okafor/Lind source. FlexWeek has a commercial conflict: its 40% headline describes the best self-rated team, while average output rose only 4.1% across 14 clients. [retraction_notices.md] [flexweek_whitepaper.md]

Cost lines sum to EUR 507,000 rather than EUR 435,000, a EUR 72,000 discrepancy. Additional support staffing costs EUR 312,000. Support has the highest burnout and 74% coverage concern, warranting separate planning. [cost_model.csv] [staff_survey.csv]

Use a time-bounded pilot with output, actual hours, wellbeing, retention and coverage checks. These small studies cannot establish company-wide gains; pilot timing and implementation detail remain unresolved. [studies/nordvik_2025.md] [studies/harlow_2025.md]
